brief:
今日财经关键词是油价、AI 算力和亚洲市场分化。中东航运遇袭与风暴叠加，油价反弹，路透引述高管称全球石油库存缓冲已几乎耗尽，WSJ 盘中记录了出口恢复与霍尔木兹海峡风险的拉锯。AI 交易上，台湾股市在 AI 热潮中超过韩国成为全球领头羊，而韩国散户在芯片巨头杠杆 ETF 上数月亏掉约 17 亿美元，狂热与风险同源。三星三季度利润预计暴涨九倍，但芯片利润率可能持平，说明存储涨价而非逻辑芯片在撑业绩。点评一句：能源为 AI 供电、AI 为股市续命，今天的财经新闻其实是同一根链条——油、电、芯片缺一不可。

items.title: Indian Opposition Leader Detained After Voter Roll Standoff
items.summary: Police in New Delhi temporarily detained key opposition leader Rahul Gandhi to end an almost nine-hour standoff during a protest seeking the resignation of the chief election official. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.title: Sanlam’s $1.2 Billion Santam Bet Puts Capital Choices in Focus
items.summary: Sanlam Ltd.’s $1.2 billion bid to take full ownership of Santam Ltd. will give Africa’s top insurer more freedom to deploy capital across the continent, India and the Lloyd’s of London market, the latest step in an expansion that will soon include banking.

items.title: Stock Rally Stalls in Asia, Bonds Dip as Oil Gains: Markets Wrap
items.summary: Asian stocks slipped, in contrast to Wall Street’s record-setting rally, as enthusiasm over the corporate earnings outlook failed to carry over to the region. Treasuries fell as oil climbed.

items.title: Japanese Beer Maker Shares Drop on Price-Fixing Probe
items.summary: Shares of Japanese beer makers fell after the nation’s competition authority started investigating them over suspected price fixing.

items.title: Can India Close Its Huge Pension Gap?
items.summary:
Fewer than 30% of Indians have access to a retirement account, even as the number of people over 60 is set to more than double by 2036. Saikat Das explains India’s pension problem and what the government is doing to fix it.
 (Source: Bloomberg)

items.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Oct. 7
items.summary: Oil gained as traders weighed increased flows through the Strait of Hormuz against a pickup in Iranian attacks against vessels.

items.title: Korean Investors Suffer $1.7 Billion Losses From Leveraged ETFs
items.summary: Retail investors are estimated to have lost 2.3 trillion won ($1.7 billion) from leveraged exchange-traded products tracking South Korea’s two chipmaking giants in just months, according to a lawmaker’s office, in the first revelation of the magnitude of risks from such bets.

items.title: QatarEnergy Secures $3 Billion Loan From Four Chinese Banks
items.summary: State-owned QatarEnergy has secured a $3 billion loan from Chinese banks, according to people familiar with the matter, another sign that financial firms are still willing to lend to certain Gulf borrowers, despite the protracted US war with Iran.

items.title: RBI Meeting Is About More Than Just Interest Rates for Markets
items.summary: Rate hike expected; traders eye more liquidity-draining measures and rupee commentary.

items.title: Taiwan Dethrones Korea Atop World Markets as AI Trade Widens
items.summary: As equity investors enter the final stretch of a pivotal year that’s propelled South Korea and Taiwan to the forefront of the global AI trade, the latter is emerging as the stronger bet.

items.title: Yemen’s Houthi Rebels Strike Two Airports in Saudi Arabia
items.summary: The attacks follow a new counteroffensive by Saudi-backed forces seeking to push the rebels back from the Red Sea coast.

items.title: Mexico’s Sheinbaum Is Getting Fed Up With Playing Nice With the U.S.
items.summary: U.S. sanctions on alleged cartel-linked officials have infuriated the president as she faces relentless pressure from the Trump administration.

items.title: ‘Preparing to Fire’: Hear the Radio Commands Enforcing the U.S. Blockade of Iran
items.summary: Audio recordings capture months of warnings, confusion and attacks in the U.S. Navy’s blockade of Iranian oil exports.

items.title: U.S. Escalates Pressure on Russia Over Siberia Lab Death
items.summary: The U.S. has warned Moscow that its failure to disclose details about the death violates international health obligations.

items.title: U.S. Presses Russia for Details on Plague Lab Death
items.summary: Plus, a former German spy chief was arrested on suspicion of espionage and Google and Constellation Energy struck a 20-year nuclear-power deal.

items.title: French Government Is Willing to Bypass Parliament to Pass Billions in Cuts
items.summary: In an interview, French Finance Minister Roland Lescure said he is open to negotiation but will do “whatever it takes” to get the budget through.

items.title: FlyDubai Attacker Was Part of Pilot Hiring Spree at Fast-Growing Airline
items.summary: Authorities and industry insiders are now questioning whether the airline’s fast growth contributed to last week’s near catastrophe.

items.title: Oil Futures Little Changed as Market Weighs Export Recovery, Shipping Risks
items.summary: Oil prices staged a late recovery Tuesday, snapping a two-session losing streak as traders assessed recovering Middle East crude exports against fresh shipping incidents around the Strait of Hormuz and renewed fighting near the Bab al-Mandeb Strait.

items.title: Families of Dead Prospectors Sue Authority That Certifies Gold as Ethically Produced
items.summary: The claimants said that after the killings, the London Bullion Market Association should have withheld stamp of approval for a Tanzanian mine.

items.title: Hackers Use Chinese AI Tool to Hit South Korean Banks, Exposing New Risk
items.summary: The attacks were the latest to highlight the vulnerability of even hardened targets to hackers using freely available artificial-intelligence tools.
